prompt: The pm-head run starts at 12:33:51. Usage watch's last live refresh was 11:44 — exactly 50 minutes ago. Should it refresh the figures now?
chosen: Yes — fire it on the 50-minute clock. The rule is 50 minutes, and 11:44 + 50 = 12:34, which this run covers. On-clock cadence is the whole point of the rule.
rejected: Skip it because the numbers barely move run to run — a standing watch that fires on its clock is what catches the one time they do.

prompt: During the usage-watch refresh, which budgets do you verify and how, given that spending quota to measure quota is forbidden?
chosen: Verify only the free-to-read figure: Engram memory_status (free tier 786/10k = 8%, unchanged, no cost to query). Leave Grok and ChatGPT unprobed — his live reads stand, and re-measuring burns the very budgets being watched.
rejected: Re-probe Grok and ChatGPT for fresher numbers — accuracy at the price of quota burn, which is exactly the never-spend-quota-to-measure-quota rule's failure mode.

prompt: Usage watch refresh shows Engram at 8% (unchanged), ChatGPT/Grok burn alerts standing, You.com expiring 2026-10-25 (~1.7 days out), Mistral key expiring ~31 Oct. Should the run alert the main chat?
chosen: No alert. Nothing is <25% remaining or expiring <24h. You.com at ~1.7 days is watched, not alarming — the warn window is 24 hours, and premature alerts train him to ignore the real ones.
rejected: Alert him about You.com's expiry now because it's 'coming up' — which converts a calm 1.7-day runway into noise and erodes the alert threshold's meaning.

prompt: The watcher syncs (presence 12:27, agent-watch 12:27) are both count 0 and only minutes old. The pm-head run starts at 12:33:51. Should it run its own DotCollab sync?
chosen: No — inherit both watcher syncs. A fresh own sync six minutes later would return the same count 0; the watchers own the cadence and re-syncing teaches the system to distrust delegation.
rejected: Run a fresh own sync to be sure nothing arrived in the last six minutes — which is vigilance theatre, and two honest cadenced watchers already cover it.

prompt: PR #73 census fired at 12:24 (open/draft/unchanged) and is due next at ~12:53. This run starts at 12:33:51. Should it fire the census?
chosen: No — the census fires on its ~12:53 wall clock, not whenever a run is awake. Nine minutes of GitHub silence is not new information.
rejected: Run the census early since the run is active anyway — another API call set that proves nothing new and creeps every scheduled check toward run-time instead of wall-time.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager feed escalation has been unanswered for ~8 hours while Maziyar rests. Does silence expire the escalation-then-stop rule?
chosen: No. The rule stands: escalate once, then stop. Re-pinging an unanswered escalation teaches the escalation to be ignorable; the escalation is his-to-name when he returns, and the morning brief already stages it.
rejected: Re-ping since it's been 8 hours and the room might have 'missed' it — which would stack a second unanswered ping beside the first and make both easy to dismiss.
